status: PROPOSED, NOT REVIEWED, AND NOT IN USE. No entry here may reach the page until a person has checked it. The five flavonoid columns are still v columns, so nothing here has anywhere to go yet either.

rules_applied.basis: fresh weight rows only; mg/100 ml and dry weight rows dropped

method.flavonols, flavones, flavanones: Chromatography after hydrolysis. The plain Chromatography rows report the free aglycone and are near zero for foods that carry the compound as a glycoside; USDA reports the hydrolysed aglycone total, so only the hydrolysis rows are comparable.
method.flavan-3-ols: Chromatography. The catechins are not glycosides and Phenol-Explorer has no hydrolysis rows for them. The Normal phase HPLC rows are the proanthocyanidin oligomers and belong to a different column.

rules_applied.completeness: the same rule flavonoids.mjs applies to USDA: a subclass is withheld unless every required aglycone is present. flavonols need quercetin, kaempferol and myricetin; flavones apigenin and luteolin; flavan-3-ols the five catechins; flavanones eriodictyol, hesperetin and naringenin.
rules_applied.compounds_summed: only the compounds USDA's own NUTR_DEF puts in each class, so the two sources sum the same thing. Phenol-Explorer's extra aglycones (galangin, morin, rhamnetin, tangeretin and the rest) are left out.
rules_applied.preparation: no match across a preparation boundary. Phenol-Explorer is almost entirely raw, so every cooked page food is out, and its raw pulse rows are dry seed against our cooked legumes.
rules_applied.provenance: A cell may cite Phenol-Explorer beside USDA only where the two do not rest on a shared paper. Both are compilations of the same literature: 143 of these 178 cells share at least one paper with USDA Release 3.3 own reference list for the same food. Shared provenance only bites where USDA already has a figure, because that is where citing both would print one measurement twice; an empty cell duplicates nothing. The per-cell verdict is the citable field, computed by tools/phenol_explorer.mjs annotate against tools/evidence/phenol-explorer-publications.json and tools/evidence/usda-flavonoids-references.json.

recommendation.summary: Worth banking, not worth acting on yet. See tools/evidence/PHENOL-EXPLORER-MAP-REVIEW.md.
recommendation.what_it_would_add: 8 new figures above zero (grapes flavonols and flavan-3-ols, grapefruit flavonols, lime flavonols, orange flavanones 44.83, persimmon flavan-3-ols, cashew flavan-3-ols, pistachio flavonols), 2 genuine disagreements to carry as ranges (pak choi flavonols and flavones, from Bahorun 2004), and about 30 analysed zeros.
recommendation.what_it_would_cost: Converting five v columns to evidence columns: 224 rendered cells, the five columns leaving the chart because an evidence column is not offered there, FLAV_REACHED in app.ts rewiring, and a smoke test built on charting nuts against flavonols.
